question: The input data is raw paired-end FASTQ files (6 samples, not yet quantified) that must be aligned/pseudo-aligned to a reference and summarized into a gene-level count matrix before any differential expression test can run. I confirmed against the package census and via targeted checks that no read aligner or pseudo-aligner is available in this sandbox (STAR, HISAT2, salmon, kallisto, bowtie2, bwa, and the R equivalent Rsubread are all absent from Python pip, R CRAN, R Bioconductor, and R GitHub inventories). DESeq2/edgeR/limma are present but they consume a counts matrix, not FASTQ. Reference-wise, a GRCh38 GENCODE v50 GTF is available but there is no matching genome FASTA or a pre-built alignment/pseudoalignment index for human in /mnt/refs. Without either (a) a quantification tool being provisioned in the sandbox, or (b) the samples being re-supplied as a pre-computed gene/transcript count matrix, the differential-expression question cannot be answered — every DE step would only be able to report failure. Please provision a read aligner/pseudoaligner (e.g., STAR, salmon, or kallisto) plus a matching genome/transcriptome reference, or supply the data as a count matrix instead of raw FASTQ, so a valid plan can proceed.
